intro: When you search for a divorce solicitor near me, you are likely looking for clear, local guidance through a difficult time. A divorce solicitor can explain the no-fault divorce process, help you reach a financial settlement, and advise on arrangements for children. We introduce you to a suitable UK solicitor who will quote you directly, with fees on application.
need_heading: What people searching for a divorce solicitor near me usually need
need_lead: Most people want a solicitor who can explain the process clearly and help them make fair, lasting decisions.
needs: You want to understand how the no-fault divorce process works and what steps are involved from start to finish.
You need advice on reaching a financial settlement that is fair and provides certainty for the future.
You are concerned about arrangements for children and want guidance on what is reasonable and how to agree it.
You are unsure whether mediation is required before going to court and want to know your options.
You want to ensure full financial disclosure is handled properly so that any agreement is robust.
context: Divorce itself does not end financial claims between you and your former partner; only a financial order can do that. A solicitor can help you apply for a financial order so that the settlement is legally binding and gives you both certainty.

Mediation is usually required before a court will consider certain applications, and it can help you reach agreement without going to court. Full financial disclosure is essential so that any settlement is based on an accurate picture of both parties' finances.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Mention that you are looking for a divorce solicitor near you and whether you prefer someone in your local area.
Briefly describe your situation, such as whether the divorce is agreed or contested, and whether you have already started proceedings.
Say whether you need help with financial arrangements, children's arrangements, or both.
Let us know if you have already tried mediation or if a court application is involved.
Indicate if there are particular issues such as a family business, property, or pensions that need to be considered.
Tell us your preferred way of working, such as meeting in person or communicating remotely, so we can introduce you to a suitable solicitor.
questions_heading: Questions to ask the divorce solicitor
questions: What are your fees and how will you keep me informed about costs as the matter progresses?
How will you help me achieve a fair financial settlement, and what information will you need from me?
What is your approach to arrangements for children, and how do you involve them in the process?
Will you recommend mediation, and how does that work alongside the divorce process?
How will you ensure full financial disclosure from both sides, and what happens if there is a dispute?
What is the likely timeline for my case, and what are the key milestones I should expect?

faqs.q: Do I need a solicitor to get divorced?
faqs.a: You can apply for a divorce without a solicitor, but a solicitor can guide you through the process, help you avoid common pitfalls, and advise on financial and children matters. Many people find that professional advice saves time and reduces stress.

faqs.q: What is a financial order and why do I need one?
faqs.a: A financial order is a legally binding court order that sets out how finances are divided. Without one, your former partner could potentially make a financial claim against you in the future, even after the divorce is finalised.

faqs.q: Is mediation compulsory before I can go to court?
faqs.a: In many cases, you will be expected to attend a mediation information and assessment meeting before a court will hear certain applications. Mediation can help you reach agreement without the expense and stress of court.

faqs.q: How do I check that a solicitor is properly regulated?
faqs.a: Solicitors in England and Wales are regulated by the Solicitors Regulation Authority (SRA), and you can check an individual or firm on the SRA's register. In Scotland, check with the Law Society of Scotland, and in Northern Ireland with the Law Society of Northern Ireland.

extra: Searching for a divorce solicitor near me suggests you value being able to meet in person and have someone local who understands the practicalities of your area, such as local court arrangements. It may also mean you want the option of face-to-face meetings for sensitive discussions. When you contact solicitors, ask how they usually communicate and whether they offer appointments at times that suit you.

To compare solicitors, look at their published information and ask about their experience in divorce and financial matters. You can check whether a solicitor is regulated by the Solicitors Regulation Authority (SRA) in England and Wales, the Law Society of Scotland, or the Law Society of Northern Ireland, depending on where you are. It is also worth asking about their approach to mediation and how they keep costs transparent.

At a first appointment, a divorce solicitor will typically ask about your circumstances, explain the no-fault divorce process, and outline the steps involved. They may discuss financial disclosure and the importance of a financial order, as well as arrangements for children. Come prepared with key dates and any documents you have, and don't be afraid to ask questions about fees and what happens next.

extra_faqs.q: How do I check if a divorce solicitor is properly regulated?
extra_faqs.a: In England and Wales, solicitors are regulated by the Solicitors Regulation Authority (SRA), and you can check an individual or firm on the SRA's register. In Scotland, check with the Law Society of Scotland, and in Northern Ireland with the Law Society of Northern Ireland.

extra_faqs.q: What should I bring to my first meeting with a divorce solicitor?
extra_faqs.a: It helps to bring any relevant documents, such as your marriage certificate, details of your finances, and any correspondence from your former partner or the court. A brief timeline of key events can also be useful. The solicitor will guide you through what else they need.
